declared.text: confirmed when every held-out share of district-days at a level (region x season x level, June-December 2018-2025) is at most 1.5 x its development value, and at every level and reading the independent slides the rule leaves uncovered compared with R0 on the same days are at most q x 87 + 2.0 x sqrt(87 q (1 - q))

alternative.text: confirmed when every held-out share of district-days at a level (region x season x level, June-December 2018-2025) is at most 1.5 x its development value, and at every level and reading the independent slides the rule leaves uncovered compared with R0 on the same days are at most q x 87 + 2.0 x sqrt(87 q (1 - q))

caveats: Development data only (2007-2017, out of fold, every scored cell); the curve's shares are fitted leave-one-year-out. No held-out number is in the development tables.
The district levels aggregate today's published cell levels (option A: the card's thresholds and the whole live chain except the blind-escalation rule).
Catalogue events are recorded where people and roads are, and most landslides are never recorded; coverage counts recorded events only.
The chance floor is the share of district-days at the level within one day: the coverage an event placed in a random district on a random day would get. Read coverage against it.
A cost ratio counts every alerted district-day without a recorded event as a false alarm.
January-May has no held-out panels, so its rows can only ever be development numbers.
District boundaries: ODbL 1.0; contains information from geoBoundaries (gbOpen) and OpenStreetMap contributors. Nepal uses the 75 districts of 2006, Bhutan its 20 dzongkhags.
